facts.statement: Neptunidraco is the oldest known member of the metriorhynchid family of fully marine reptiles.
facts.quote: It is currently the oldest known metriorhynchid, an extinct group of fully marine reptiles related to modern crocodylians.

facts.statement: Neptunidraco lived during the Middle Jurassic period in what is now northeastern Italy.
facts.quote: Neptunidraco (meaning "Neptune's dragon") is an extinct genus of metriorhynchid thalattosuchian that lived during the middle Jurassic period (late Bajocian to earliest Bathonian stage) in what is now northeastern Italy.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Neptunidraco was recovered in the 1950s near Portomaggiore, Italy.
facts.quote: The type specimen was recovered in the 1950s near the Italian town of Portomaggiore.

facts.statement: Italian paleontologists Andrea Cau and Federico Fanti named the genus Neptunidraco in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, Italian paleontologists Andrea Cau and Federico Fanti named this specimen as the new genus Neptunidraco, containing the single species Neptunidraco ammoniticus.

facts.statement: The type specimen is a partial skeleton with an incomplete skull and mandible preserved in nodular limestone.
facts.quote: The specimen, informally known as the "Portomaggiore crocodile", comprises a partial skeleton, including an incomplete skull with mandible, preserved in nodular limestone of the Rosso Ammonitico Veronese Formation.

facts.statement: The Neptunidraco specimen is the most complete metriorhynchid known from Italy.
facts.quote: It represents the most complete metriorhynchid specimen known from Italy.

facts.statement: Neptunidraco belongs to the subfamily Geosaurinae, which consists of large marine predators adapted to open-ocean life.
facts.quote: Neptunidraco is a member of the metriorhynchid subfamily called Geosaurinae, a group generally consisting of large marine predators that were adapted to open-ocean life.

facts.statement: Neptunidraco is an extinct carnivorous marine crocodilian that lived during the Middle Jurassic in northeastern Italy.
facts.quote: Neptunidraco (que significa dragón de "Neptuno") es un género extinto de crocodiliforme marino carnívoro que vivió durante el período geológico Jurásico Medio (finales del Bajociano a principios del periodo Bathoniense) en lo que ahora es el noreste de Italia.

facts.statement: Before its formal description, the Neptunidraco specimen was referred to as an unnamed species of the genera Metriorhynchus or Geosaurus.
facts.quote: Este espécimen había sido previamente referido como una especie no nombrada de los géneros Metriorhynchus o Geosaurus del Jurásico tardío.

facts.statement: The time range for Neptunidraco is estimated from 170.9 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Tithonian (170.9 to 143.1 million years ago)

rejected.statement: A 2023 study suggests that a specimen previously linked to Neptunidraco actually belongs to a separate indeterminate metriorhynchid.
rejected.quote: In 2013, Cau suggested that the possible specimen of this genus, MGP-PD 26552... would have measured 3.7 m in total body length, though the 2023 study suggested that the specimen belongs to a separate indeterminate metriorhynchid.

rejected.quote: It is closely related to, but not part of, the more derived tribe Geosaurini, whose members were the largest and exhibited the most pronounced morphological adaptations for predation on large-bodied prey.
